title: Welcome to ACT: Finding Your Challenge Zone
main_theme: Program orientation and the introduction of the 'three learning zones' (comfort / challenge / pain) framework that recurs throughout ACT.
main_question_note: Not explicitly stated in either source. Lesson 1 functions as an orientation lesson (welcome, program overview, safe space, baseline survey, and the zones-of-learning framework), not a chapter lesson with its own guiding question. See review-notes.md.
video_duration_policy: All ACT lesson videos must fall between 5 and 20 minutes (project-wide constraint).
objectives: Break the ice and help participants get to know each other
Introduce participants to the Community Leaders Program (ACT) - its philosophy, structure, and the organizations behind it
Create a safe space where participants feel free to share thoughts and opinions
Evaluate participants' existing knowledge of the program before it begins
Motivate participants to engage with the material and adopt a growth-oriented spirit by understanding the three learning zones
Instill the mindset that challenges are what sharpen our skills
main_outcomes: Participants get to know each other and discover what they have in common
Participants form a positive first impression of the program
Participants understand the CLP's philosophy and the entities behind it (executing, hosting, organizing)
Participants get to know the trainer's background and expertise
Participants feel motivated about the program's material
Participants collaboratively set the rules that govern respectful, open participation and understand they are decision-makers who shape how the program runs
Participants' baseline knowledge of the program is recorded for later comparison
Participants open their appetite for learning and are prepared to face challenges in life and future projects
Participants are introduced to the idea of broadening their scope of skills and capabilities
Participants are motivated to treat obstacles as challenges and to deliberately step outside their comfort zone
Participants recognize that the challenge zone is the learning zone, where skills develop
parallel_outcomes: Participants become motivated to face challenges generally, and to accept and coexist with the challenges of their society

activities.summary: Write three things about yourself (a hobby, a skill, a trait) on three small papers; originally exchanged and discussed with other participants in person.
Program overview: philosophy, 4-unit structure, organizations involved (NAMA Foundation, Ghadan, NICE), trainer self-introduction via 'two truths and a lie'.
Establish shared ground rules for open, respectful participation; originally a live group vote and signed flipchart.
Ungraded baseline knowledge survey. Actual survey questions missing from supplied source - see review-notes.md.

Introduces the comfort/challenge/pain zone framework via five scenario questions, a four-phase reflective discussion, and a motivational closing speech (includes a religious reference - see review-notes.md).

activities.original_name: Short Motivational Video - The Koh Panyee Island Soccer Team (Thailand). Note: the source schedule table and its matching slide title label this the 'Taiwan Team'; resolved to 'Thailand' based on the activity's own detailed description and the film's identity - see review-notes.md.
activities.summary: The Koh Panyee Island Soccer Team short film, linked out rather than embedded (to sidestep unclear third-party licensing and keep this lesson's own video inside the 5-20 minute policy), followed by discussion questions and a closing group affirmation.

key_takeaways: Growth happens in the challenge zone, not the comfort zone, and ACT is intentionally designed to keep you there.
The comfort/challenge/pain framework introduced here recurs throughout the whole program.
This lesson establishes the emotional and practical groundwork (welcome, trust, safety, shared rules) the rest of the program stands on.
